# What the rebase onto main broke, and the drift it exposed underneath

RED is record 55 and GREEN is record 56, `test_loop.py` at 43 passed with 6 subtests. The RED is the failure the
rebase produced, recorded as it stood: `AttributeError: module 'harness.handoff' has no attribute
'accepted_greens'`, reached from `_tdd` through `_before_the_tdd_gate` into `_regression`.

**It was a semantic conflict, and only the suite found it.** SEEN-113 merged to main today and its F3 fix removed
`handoff.accepted_greens`, replacing it with `slices_proved`, because counting greens let rework after a replan
advance the count past a slice nobody had worked. SEEN-112's `loop.py` still called the removed function. Git
merged the two branches without a murmur, because they touch different files; nothing but running the tests would
have said so, and nine commits rebased cleanly.

**`_regression` needed a position, not a count, and not the greens.** The tdd gate's rule is that a slice's green
sequence is at or before the regression's, so the only question is which record a regression must follow.
`slices_proved` answers how far into the plan the work has got, and a plan proved to two of three says nothing
about which record the regression must come after: a count is not a sequence. So `loop.py` has a local
`_last_green` returning **one sequence number**, and two differences from the function it replaces are argued in
the code rather than left implicit. It returns a sequence and never a list, because a list of greens invites being
counted, which is the defect SEEN-113 removed and which must not come back into the tree under another name. And
it is unscoped by the plan, because the tdd gate decides a citation by the tree a check ran against rather than by
which acceptance came first, so a record may cite a green older than the acceptance `plan_accepted_at` now starts
at; sequences only grow, so the last green of the journal is the last green of the plan wherever the plan has one,
and where it has none this is the stricter reading of the same rule. `_regression` no longer calls into `handoff`
at all.

**The guard was proved to bite rather than asserted.** `RegressionOrderTest` drives three cases through
`harness run` rather than against the private function: the regression is what the loop asks for once the plan is
proved and measured, a regression recorded before the green it covers does not count and the loop asks again, and
one recorded after it sends the run on. The implementer temporarily set the comparison to zero and re-ran: the
before-the-green test failed with `AssertionError: 'draft' != 'check'` and the other two passed, so the test
distinguishes the fix from its absence. The edit was reverted before the GREEN.

**And one drift the walk found, reported rather than fixed.** Every `handoff`, `gates`, `routing`, `journal` and
`github` attribute `loop.py` uses was checked against the live modules by parsing rather than by grep, and
`accepted_greens` was the only removed name. But `handoff.plan_accepted_at` survived with a **changed meaning**:
SEEN-113 made it return the first acceptance of the plan that still stands rather than the last. `loop.py` calls
it twice more. In `citations` the wider window is what SEEN-113 wants and the behaviour improves. In
`_second_return` the docstring still says a replan that passes the solution gate again starts its own count, which
is now only half true, because a return to solution re-accepting the same slices no longer resets it and returns
accumulate across it. Nothing crashes and it is arguably the stricter reading of thrashing, but the comment and
the behaviour have drifted apart, and a ticket whose own criterion 3 names a second return as a stop should not
carry a stale description of how it counts them.
